question: In your research system, the web search subagent is configured with two MCP servers: a web search server and a citation lookup server. During one task, the subagent must find sources and then confirm the publication details of each source. A teammate claims that the subagent can reach the tools of only one MCP server at a time, and he proposes a change to the design. What should you do?

options.text: Build a custom wrapper MCP server that re-exposes the tools of both servers, so that the subagent connects to a single server only.
options.reason: The wrapper rests on the false idea of one server at a time; the guide says tools from all configured servers are available together, and it reserves custom servers for team-specific workflows.

options.text: Split the web search subagent into two subagents that each have one MCP server, and have the coordinator pass the found sources from the first subagent to the second.
options.reason: One agent already gets the tools of all its configured MCP servers at the same time, so splitting the subagent adds complexity to solve a problem that does not exist.

options.text: Disconnect the web search server after the search step and connect the citation lookup server, so that its tools are discovered for the verification step.
options.reason: The guide says tools from all configured servers are discovered at connection time and are available together, so swapping servers between steps is unnecessary.

options.text: Keep both servers configured as they are, because tools from both servers are discovered at connection time and are available to the subagent together.
options.reason: The guide states that tools from all configured MCP servers are discovered at connection time and are available to the agent at the same time, so no change is needed.
